about.title: Agoura Hills Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Agoura Hills residents rely on a mix of local urgent care clinics and larger medical centers along the US-101 corridor and nearby Conejo Valley communities for everything from routine checkups to major surgery. Most of the time, care goes as expected. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mishandles medication, the consequences can follow a patient for years. California law sets a fairly narrow window and specific procedural steps for pursuing these claims, which makes early guidance valuable. We don't charge any fee to review your case — our team handles medical malpractice claims and can evaluate whether a bad medical outcome may have crossed into negligence. If you or a family member were harmed during treatment, it costs nothing to have your situation reviewed by someone who understands how these cases work in California.

whyChoose.title: Why Agoura Hills Families Choose Us

items.title: MICRA Deadlines Are Unforgiving
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discovered the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to act — plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice. Missing either step can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Damage Caps Require Careful Case-Building
items.desc: California law caps non-economic damages, though the cap rises each year under current law. Our team, familiar with this framework, can help make sure your economic losses are properly documented alongside it.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A qualified medical expert typically has to confirm that care fell below the accepted standard — a bad outcome by itself isn't enough. Contacting us early gives more time to gather records and line up that review.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a mandatory 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed. Because these rules are strict, it's worth having your timeline reviewed as soon as possible.

items.question: My surgery in Agoura Hills didn't go the way I expected — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. A poor outcome alone doesn't establish negligence under California law; a qualified medical expert generally has to show the care fell below the accepted standard. We can help evaluate your medical records to see whether that standard was met.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes, California law caps non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, though that cap increases annually under current statute. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are generally handled separately. Our team can walk you through how these categories apply to your specific situation.
